evidence.description: REQ-009 requires one read-only RPC transaction for all four organ row sets, and lines 115-116 unambiguously separate the single PostgREST request contract from filtering inside the SQL function, closing iteration-3 FIND-001.
Lines 12-14 mirror the one-RPC body, internal tenant/organ/half-open filters, complete-or-overflow result, and service-only execution contract.

REQ-008 defines a caller-issued non-zero revision key, the exact uniqueness tuple, exact-retry success, changed-payload conflict, and fresh-key status re-entry and same-status correction, closing iteration-3 FIND-002.
The source contract mirrors retry/conflict and re-entry/correction semantics and supplies deterministic organ-specific winner rules.

REQ-009 pins SECURITY INVOKER, a fixed search_path, table SELECT and function EXECUTE to service_role, revokes browser-role access, and binds p_uid only after session authentication, closing iteration-3 FIND-003.
The query-shell design independently repeats the function security, table privileges, function privileges, and authenticated endpoint UID binding.
Lines 5-21 keep deterministic scoring in the pure core while isolating authenticated querying, persistence, presentation, and release readback in explicit effectful shells.
Lines 149-153 define the same purity boundary and prohibit score derivation or mutation in the read shell.

Lines 84-85 name an executable PostgreSQL 18 command and artifact and require real roles, migration application, concurrent psql sessions, access denials, idempotency/conflict/re-entry checks, and actual limit/overflow cases, closing iteration-3 FIND-004.
PROP-004 and PROP-005 make the executable database security, snapshot, overflow, idempotency, append-only, and grant checks required proof obligations.
